'''Ikzen''' is a [[Wikipedia:landlocked country|landlocked nation]] situated in [[North Ayuma]]. About 1% of Ikzen's territory, west of the [[Tusil river]], borders [[Estijan]] to the north, [[Areoix Lie]] to the east, [[Ealdorii]] to the south, and [[Urbiqu]] to the west. The capital is [[Velotha]], and the country's [[List of most populous cities in Ikzen|largest city]] and principal cultural and economic center is [[Vashkiri]], which served as the capital until 1741.
  
Ikzen is the world's [[List of countries and dependencies by area|seventeenth-largest country by land area]] and the third largest landlocked country. The [[Untschalle|Untschalle Steppe]] and [[Taiylsh Desert]] account for nearly half of its vast territory, with the [[Valmiran Mountains]] composing the rest. Ikzen has a population of 3.1 million and [[List of countries and dependencies by population density|one of the lowest population densities]] in the world, with fewer than {{convert|4|/km2|/mi2|disp=preunit|people&nbsp;|people|}}.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://ikz.ikzrsiv.media/ral/2763-11-16/Ikzens-population-reaches-3-million |title=Ikzen's population reaches 20 million}</ref> Ethnic [[Seljan]] constitute a majority, living along the banks of the [[Tusil River]] with the [[Ikzener]]s, inhabit the while steppes and desserts, [[Estijan in Ikzen|ethnic Estijan]] form a small minority around the capital reigon. Officially secular, Ikzen is a [[Kelhari|Kelhari-majority country]] with a sizeable [[Tzinalli community]].

In antiquity, various nomadic [[Tainabide peoples]] such as the [[Taiylsh]], and later [[Duhmi]], dominated the territory, with the [[Ukhdari Empire]] expanding towards the south in [[Alzuri (region)|Alzuria]]. [[Duhmi peoples|Duhmi]] nomads entered the region from the sixth century. In the 7th century, the area was subjugated by the [[Yethran Empire]], and many Alzurians migrated up along the Tusil river. Following the disintegration of the [[Usstela Elunt]] in the 12th century, the [[Kingdom of Selja]] was established over an area roughly corresponding with the modern populated areas of Ikzen. By the start of the 14th century, the [[Ezhinads]] had conquered the area. After the [[Seniaaii Wars]] and the [[Treaty of Brimasha]], the modern areas of Ikzen were conquered by the [[Estijan Huan]]; by the mid-[[17th century]], all of Ikzen was nominally under Estijan rule.<ref>{{cite web |last=Glialiev |first=Anuar |date=1734 |title=Traditional Institutions in Modern Ikzen |url=http://src-h.slav.hokudai.ac.est.aas.sympo/34.summer/galiev.html |url-status=live}}</ref>. It was granted the status of a "state" within the Huan in 1678. The Huan government settled many [[Seljan|Seljans]] from [[Ealdorii]] in the province, resulting in ethnic Ikzeners becoming a minority during the Huan era. Ikzen was the first Huan state to declare independence in 1739 during the [[Collapse of the Huan]], gaining full independence in 1741.

Ikzen is a [[wikipedia:Unitary parliamentary republic|Unitary semi-parliamentary republic]] consisting of [[Regions of Ikzen|nine provinces]]. [[Seljan language |Seljan]] is the official language of the nations, with [[Ikzener language|Ikzener]] and [[Estijan language|Estijan]] recognized as regional languages and the official inter-ethnic language.<ref>{{cite web | url=https://www.bestitannica.com/topic/Seljan-people | title=Seljan &#124; North and Central Ayuman languages &#124; Britannica }}</ref> It is a [[wikipedia:developing country|developing country]] with a [[wikipedia:Transition economy|transitional economy]] that is dependent on [[wikipedia:remittance]]s and on the production of [[diamonds]] and [[Giaven]].
